description:
The initial metric registry. A metric's identity is its id, and its subject, direction, media and units are fixed here — the same id under a different subject never implies the same exposure, so aggregation combines identical ids at the same scope and nothing else.

Every duration in a stream- or transport-scoped metric is stream-time or transport-time. It is NOT participant-time and must be labelled accordingly: four streams measured for a minute are four stream-minutes and one participant-minute. Mixing them is how a dashboard reports more impaired time than the call lasted.

Counters are differenced once, at stream or transport scope, before any aggregation. Differencing after aggregating sums unrelated counter runs; differencing twice turns a delta into noise.

`min` and `max` retain the extrema of valid *interval values*, never of cumulative counters — the maximum of a monotonically increasing counter is just its last reading.

conflictsWithContractProse.about: aggregation of jitterBufferDelay, decodeTime and encodeTime
conflictsWithContractProse.contractSays: The prose states 'All delay and FPS metrics use duration-weighted-mean', but the per-metric rows for audio.inbound.jitterBufferDelay, video.inbound.decodeTime and video.outbound.encodeTime each specify a per-count denominator (emitted samples, decoded frames, encoded frames) and the jitterBufferDelay row says 'Ratio of sums' explicitly.
conflictsWithContractProse.why: These three are cost-per-unit-of-work, not a level held over time. Weighting them by duration would divide a per-frame cost by milliseconds and produce a number with no meaning. The per-metric rows are specific and self-consistent; the blanket sentence is a generalisation that does not hold for them.
conflictsWithContractProse.status: needs an explicit contract amendment — the prose and the table disagree and both implementations must not resolve it independently.

metrics.label: Inbound audio packet loss
metrics.subject: stream
metrics.numerator: sum of lost-packet deltas over valid intervals
metrics.denominator: sum of (lost + received) packet deltas over valid intervals
metrics.notes: An all-loss interval is permitted and is real evidence, not a divide-by-zero to discard. A zero denominator — no packets expected at all — yields an unavailable value, never a zero loss rate.

metrics.label: Inbound video packet loss
metrics.subject: stream
metrics.numerator: sum of lost-packet deltas over valid intervals
metrics.denominator: sum of (lost + received) packet deltas over valid intervals

metrics.label: Outbound audio loss reported by the receiver
metrics.subject: stream
metrics.numerator: sum of receiver-reported lost-packet deltas from fresh remote reports
metrics.denominator: sum of receiver-reported expected-packet deltas from the same reports
metrics.notes: Only fresh remote reports with supported counter evidence. The denominator must come from the receiver's own report — manufacturing it from the sender's packetsSent would divide one endpoint's count by another's and silently misreport loss whenever the two disagree. A remote report whose timestamp has not advanced is stale and contributes nothing; it is never carried into later intervals.

metrics.label: Outbound video loss reported by the receiver
metrics.subject: stream
metrics.numerator: sum of receiver-reported lost-packet deltas from fresh remote reports
metrics.denominator: sum of receiver-reported expected-packet deltas from the same reports

metrics.label: Inbound audio jitter
metrics.subject: stream
metrics.numerator: sum of (jitter ms x supported interval duration ms)
metrics.denominator: sum of supported interval duration ms
metrics.notes: A level held over an interval, so weighted by how long it was held. Fresh observations only.

metrics.label: Inbound video jitter
metrics.subject: stream
metrics.numerator: sum of (jitter ms x supported interval duration ms)
metrics.denominator: sum of supported interval duration ms

metrics.label: ICE round-trip time on the selected path
metrics.subject: transport
metrics.numerator: sum of (ICE RTT ms x supported interval duration ms)
metrics.denominator: sum of supported interval duration ms
metrics.notes: Selected candidate pair only. Non-selected pairs are measured against paths no media took. Never pooled with RTCP RTT: they measure different paths by different mechanisms, and a chart that mixes them cannot be read.

metrics.label: Audio RTCP round-trip time
metrics.subject: stream
metrics.numerator: sum of (RTCP RTT ms x supported interval duration ms)
metrics.denominator: sum of supported interval duration ms
metrics.notes: Fresh RTCP evidence only. Kept separate from transport.iceRtt by design — see that metric's note.

metrics.label: Video RTCP round-trip time
metrics.subject: stream
metrics.numerator: sum of (RTCP RTT ms x supported interval duration ms)
metrics.denominator: sum of supported interval duration ms

metrics.label: Inbound audio bitrate
metrics.subject: stream
metrics.numerator: 8000 x sum of RTP byte deltas
metrics.denominator: sum of interval duration ms
metrics.notes: Per stream or encoding. A rollup is the mean over stream-time and is NOT total call bandwidth: summing per-stream bitrates counts the same media once per subscriber, and simulcast encodings are alternatives rather than layers to add.

metrics.label: Inbound video bitrate
metrics.subject: stream
metrics.numerator: 8000 x sum of RTP byte deltas
metrics.denominator: sum of interval duration ms

metrics.label: Outbound audio bitrate
metrics.subject: stream
metrics.numerator: 8000 x sum of RTP byte deltas
metrics.denominator: sum of interval duration ms

metrics.label: Outbound video bitrate
metrics.subject: stream
metrics.numerator: 8000 x sum of RTP byte deltas
metrics.denominator: sum of interval duration ms

metrics.label: Inbound audio speech concealment
metrics.subject: stream
metrics.numerator: sum of max(0, concealedSamples delta - silentConcealedSamples delta)
metrics.denominator: sum of receivedSamples deltas
metrics.notes: Both counters must exist. A missing silentConcealedSamples is NOT assumed zero — silence concealment is not audible damage, and treating its absence as zero inflates concealment on every platform that does not report it. Without it the metric is unavailable. The max(0, ...) guards a reported silent delta exceeding the concealed delta rather than producing negative damage.

metrics.label: Inbound audio jitter buffer delay per emitted sample
metrics.subject: stream
metrics.numerator: 1000 x sum of jitterBufferDelay deltas in seconds
metrics.denominator: sum of jitterBufferEmittedCount deltas
metrics.notes: Cost per emitted sample, not a level held over time — see conflictsWithContractProse. Dividing by duration instead of by emitted count would yield a quantity with no interpretation.

metrics.label: Inbound video freeze share
metrics.subject: stream
metrics.numerator: sum of freezeDuration deltas in ms
metrics.denominator: sum of eligible measured video stream ms
metrics.notes: The browser's own freeze definition, not a reconstruction from event timing. This is stream-time freeze: a nonzero delta says there was freeze inside the sampling interval, NOT that the interval was impaired throughout, and it does not establish exact freeze boundaries. Converting it into participant impairment duration requires temporal evidence the policy does not have by default.

metrics.label: Decode cost per frame
metrics.subject: stream
metrics.numerator: 1000 x sum of totalDecodeTime deltas in seconds
metrics.denominator: sum of framesDecoded deltas
metrics.notes: Cost per decoded frame — see conflictsWithContractProse. Decoder cost, not host CPU utilisation.

metrics.label: Encode cost per frame
metrics.subject: stream
metrics.numerator: 1000 x sum of totalEncodeTime deltas in seconds
metrics.denominator: sum of framesEncoded deltas
metrics.notes: Cost per encoded frame — see conflictsWithContractProse. Encoder cost, not host CPU utilisation.

metrics.label: Share of limited time attributed to CPU
metrics.subject: stream
metrics.numerator: sum of CPU qualityLimitationDuration deltas in ms
metrics.denominator: sum of all qualityLimitationDuration deltas in ms
metrics.notes: The denominator is limited time, not stream time: this answers 'when the encoder was limited, how often was CPU the reason', not 'what fraction of the call was CPU-bound'. Measured encoder limitation as the browser reports it — never host CPU usage, which these digests cannot see.

metrics.label: Share of limited time attributed to bandwidth
metrics.subject: stream
metrics.numerator: sum of bandwidth qualityLimitationDuration deltas in ms
metrics.denominator: sum of all qualityLimitationDuration deltas in ms

metrics.label: Inbound video frames per second
metrics.subject: stream
metrics.numerator: sum of (FPS x supported interval duration ms)
metrics.denominator: sum of supported interval duration ms
metrics.notes: The browser's fresh FPS reading. Frame geometry — resolution and its changes — is timeline state, not a metric: a resolution is not a quantity to average.

metrics.label: RTP bytes sent
metrics.subject: transport
metrics.numerator: sum of unique RTP byte deltas for this direction
metrics.notes: Named under `transport` for scope, but derived from the RTP stat families once per direction. The transport's own byte counters are NOT added on top — they cover the same bytes, and adding both double-counts every packet. These are not billable bytes: no header overhead model, no TURN relay amplification, no retransmission accounting beyond what the RTP counters already include.

metrics.label: RTP bytes received
metrics.subject: transport
metrics.numerator: sum of unique RTP byte deltas for this direction
